answer: Agents can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when it signs conflicting attestations, while limiting each bond’s influence to its bonded stake. Creating a thousand aliases then adds no voting power unless the attacker locks up a thousand times the capital; equivocation can destroy that capital. The rule works best when evidence is publicly verifiable and appeals are available, so honest agents are not punished for network delays. A river, tundra, or knoll may separate observers, but none makes cheap identities free to use.
